core_claim: Temporal quantum correlations can violate entanglement monogamy — a foundational constraint of spatial quantum mechanics. In a tripartite temporal process, all three pairwise CHSH inequalities can be violated simultaneously (S_AB > 2, S_BC > 2, S_AC > 2), which is impossible for any spatial tripartite quantum state.
key_insights: Temporal correlations are NOT spatial correlations in disguise — they are a distinct resource with richer structure
The process matrix formalism (double Hilbert space) reveals that not all spatial states have temporal analogs, and vice versa
Time in quantum mechanics is not merely a parameter but a structural resource that can carry correlations inaccessible to spatial configurations

sandbox_test.method: Verified spatial monogamy bound (Toner-Verstraete) forbids simultaneous violation of all three pairwise CHSH inequalities for any tripartite quantum state. Confirmed process matrices are not constrained by this bound.

results.spatial_monogamy_bound: If S_AB > 2 and S_BC > 2, then S_AC <= 2 (proven theorem)
results.conclusion: Temporal correlations violate a fundamental constraint of spatial quantum mechanics

meta_patterns.relevance: Monogamy constraint (dominant mode in spatial correlations) is suppressed in temporal domain, allowing richer correlation structures

relation_to_user_source: The user's passage is a sensationalized distortion of this real result. The actual science is more subtle and more profound: not 'time looping back,' but time as a distinct quantum resource with richer correlation structure than space.
